title: Employees earning more than their department average
prompt: Return employee_name, department_id, and salary for every employee whose salary is greater than the average salary of employees in the same department. Sort by department_id and salary descending.
hint: Calculate the department average in a correlated subquery or CTE, then compare each employee's salary to it.
sql: SELECT e.employee_name,e.department_id,e.salary FROM employees e WHERE e.salary > (SELECT AVG(x.salary) FROM employees x WHERE x.department_id=e.department_id) ORDER BY e.department_id,e.salary DESC;

title: Second highest distinct salary
prompt: Find the second highest distinct salary in the employees table. Return one column named second_highest_salary.
hint: First identify the maximum salary, then find the maximum salary below it. Think about duplicate salaries.
sql: SELECT MAX(salary) AS second_highest_salary FROM employees WHERE salary < (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employees);

title: Top 3 earners in every department
prompt: For every department, return employee_name, department_id, salary and salary_rank. Include employees whose DENSE_RANK is 3 or less within their department. Sort by department_id and salary_rank.
hint: Use DENSE_RANK() with PARTITION BY department_id and ORDER BY salary DESC.
sql: SELECT employee_name,department_id,salary,salary_rank FROM (SELECT employee_name,department_id,salary,DENSE_RANK() OVER(PARTITION BY department_id ORDER BY salary DESC) AS salary_rank FROM employees) x WHERE salary_rank<=3 ORDER BY department_id,salary_rank,salary DESC;

title: Show each employee with their manager
prompt: Display employee_name, job_title and manager_name for every employee. Employees without a manager must still appear. Sort by employee_id.
hint: employees.manager_id points to managers.manager_id. Use a LEFT JOIN.
sql: SELECT e.employee_name,e.job_title,m.manager_name FROM employees e LEFT JOIN managers m ON e.manager_id=m.manager_id ORDER BY e.employee_id;

title: Departments with no employees
prompt: List department_id and department_name for departments that currently have no employees.
hint: LEFT JOIN departments to employees and filter where the employee key is NULL.
sql: SELECT d.department_id,d.department_name FROM departments d LEFT JOIN employees e ON d.department_id=e.department_id WHERE e.employee_id IS NULL ORDER BY d.department_id;

title: Department salary summary
prompt: For each department that has employees, return department_name, employee_count, minimum_salary, maximum_salary and average_salary rounded to 2 decimals. Sort by average_salary descending.
hint: Join the tables, GROUP BY the department, and use COUNT/MIN/MAX/AVG.
sql: SELECT d.department_name,COUNT(e.employee_id) AS employee_count,MIN(e.salary) AS minimum_salary,MAX(e.salary) AS maximum_salary,ROUND(AVG(e.salary),2) AS average_salary FROM departments d JOIN employees e ON d.department_id=e.department_id GROUP BY d.department_id,d.department_name ORDER BY average_salary DESC;

title: Find duplicate customer emails
prompt: Identify customer email addresses that appear more than once in duplicate_customers. Return email and duplicate_count, only for duplicates.
hint: GROUP BY email and filter groups with HAVING COUNT(*) > 1.
sql: SELECT email,COUNT(*) AS duplicate_count FROM duplicate_customers GROUP BY email HAVING COUNT(*)>1 ORDER BY duplicate_count DESC,email;

title: Keep only the latest customer record
prompt: For each email in duplicate_customers, return only the most recently created record. Return record_id, customer_name, email, phone, city and created_at.
hint: Use ROW_NUMBER() PARTITION BY email ORDER BY created_at DESC, then keep rn = 1.
sql: SELECT record_id,customer_name,email,phone,city,created_at FROM (SELECT d.*,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY email ORDER BY created_at DESC,record_id DESC) rn FROM duplicate_customers d) x WHERE rn=1 ORDER BY record_id;

title: Find duplicate rows but keep the first
prompt: Return every duplicate customer record that should be removed if the oldest record is retained for each email.
hint: Assign ROW_NUMBER by email ordered from oldest to newest. Rows with rn > 1 are removable duplicates.
sql: SELECT record_id,customer_name,email,created_at FROM (SELECT d.*,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY email ORDER BY created_at,record_id) rn FROM duplicate_customers d) x WHERE rn>1 ORDER BY email,created_at;

title: Customers who never placed an order
prompt: Return customer_id and customer_name for customers who have never placed an order.
hint: A LEFT JOIN with NULL order_id is one approach. NOT EXISTS is another.
sql: SELECT c.customer_id,c.customer_name FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id=o.customer_id WHERE o.order_id IS NULL ORDER BY c.customer_id;

title: Top 3 customers by delivered revenue
prompt: Using only Delivered orders, find the top 3 customers by total order revenue. Return customer_name and revenue, highest first.
hint: Join customers to orders, filter status, GROUP BY customer, SUM total_amount, ORDER BY DESC, LIMIT 3.
sql: SELECT c.customer_name,SUM(o.total_amount) AS revenue FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id=o.customer_id WHERE o.status='Delivered' GROUP BY c.customer_id,c.customer_name ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 3;

title: Products never sold
prompt: List products that do not appear in order_items at all. Return product_id and product_name.
hint: LEFT JOIN products to order_items and look for NULL matches.
sql: SELECT p.product_id,p.product_name FROM products p LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id=oi.product_id WHERE oi.product_id IS NULL ORDER BY p.product_id;

title: Calculate each order from order items
prompt: For every order_id in order_items, calculate the order total as quantity × unit_price after discount. Return order_id and calculated_total rounded to 2 decimals.
hint: The discount is a percentage. Aggregate quantity * unit_price * (1 - discount_pct/100).
sql: SELECT order_id,ROUND(SUM(quantity*unit_price*(1-discount_pct/100.0)),2) AS calculated_total FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id ORDER BY order_id;

title: Best-selling product by quantity
prompt: Find the product with the highest total quantity sold. Return product_id, product_name and total_quantity. Include all products only if needed; the final answer should contain the top product.
hint: SUM quantity per product, sort descending, then take the first row.
sql: SELECT p.product_id,p.product_name,SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id=oi.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id,p.product_name ORDER BY total_quantity DESC,p.product_id LIMIT 1;

title: Running revenue by sale date
prompt: Return each sale's sale_date, sale_id, net_amount and cumulative revenue up to that sale. Order by sale_date and sale_id.
hint: Use SUM(net_amount) OVER(ORDER BY sale_date,sale_id).
sql: SELECT sale_date,sale_id,net_amount,SUM(net_amount) OVER(ORDER BY sale_date,sale_id) AS running_revenue FROM sales ORDER BY sale_date,sale_id;

title: Previous order date for each customer
prompt: For every order, return customer_id, order_id, order_date and the customer's previous order date. The first order for a customer should have NULL.
hint: LAG(order_date) over each customer ordered by order_date.
sql: SELECT customer_id,order_id,order_date,LAG(order_date) OVER(PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date,order_id) AS previous_order_date FROM orders ORDER BY customer_id,order_date;

title: Rank employees by salary within department
prompt: Return employee_name, department_id, salary and salary_rank using DENSE_RANK within each department. Highest salary should be rank 1.
hint: DENSE_RANK() OVER(PARTITION BY department_id ORDER BY salary DESC).
sql: SELECT employee_name,department_id,salary,DENSE_RANK() OVER(PARTITION BY department_id ORDER BY salary DESC) AS salary_rank FROM employees ORDER BY department_id,salary_rank,employee_name;

title: Employees earning more than company average
prompt: Return employee_name and salary for employees whose salary is above the average salary of the entire company.
hint: Compare salary with a scalar AVG(salary) subquery.
sql: SELECT employee_name,salary FROM employees WHERE salary>(SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees) ORDER BY salary DESC;

title: Monthly sales revenue
prompt: Calculate total net sales for each month represented in sales. Return month (YYYY-MM) and revenue, sorted chronologically.
hint: In SQLite, substr(sale_date,1,7) extracts YYYY-MM.
sql: SELECT substr(sale_date,1,7) AS month,SUM(net_amount) AS revenue FROM sales GROUP BY month ORDER BY month;

title: Month-over-month revenue change
prompt: Using monthly sales revenue, show month, revenue, previous_month_revenue and growth_percent. Growth should be rounded to 2 decimals and be NULL when there is no previous month.
hint: First aggregate by month in a CTE. Then use LAG on the monthly result.
sql: WITH m AS (SELECT substr(sale_date,1,7) AS month,SUM(net_amount) AS revenue FROM sales GROUP BY month) SELECT month,revenue,LAG(revenue) OVER(ORDER BY month) AS previous_month_revenue,ROUND(100.0*(revenue-LAG(revenue) OVER(ORDER BY month))/NULLIF(LAG(revenue) OVER(ORDER BY month),0),2) AS growth_percent FROM m ORDER BY month;

title: Current SCD Type 2 records
prompt: Return the current version of every employee stored in employee_scd2. Include employee_id, department_id, job_title, salary and effective_from.
hint: The current SCD2 record is identified by is_current = 1.
sql: SELECT employee_id,department_id,job_title,salary,effective_from FROM employee_scd2 WHERE is_current=1 ORDER BY employee_id;

title: Employee history with version numbers
prompt: For each employee in employee_scd2, assign version_number starting at 1 from the oldest effective_from date. Return employee_id, version_number, job_title, salary and effective_from.
hint: ROW_NUMBER partitioned by employee_id and ordered by effective_from.
sql: SELECT employee_id,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY employee_id ORDER BY effective_from) AS version_number,job_title,salary,effective_from FROM employee_scd2 ORDER BY employee_id,effective_from;

title: Point-in-time SCD2 lookup
prompt: Find the employee_id = 1 record that was valid on 2023-06-01. Return the full SCD2 row.
hint: The date must be >= effective_from and <= effective_to. Treat a NULL effective_to as an open-ended future date.
sql: SELECT * FROM employee_scd2 WHERE employee_id=1 AND '2023-06-01'>=effective_from AND '2023-06-01'<=COALESCE(effective_to,'9999-12-31');

title: Employees whose department changed
prompt: Identify employees who have more than one SCD2 version. Return employee_id and version_count.
hint: GROUP BY employee_id and use HAVING COUNT(*) > 1.
sql: SELECT employee_id,COUNT(*) AS version_count FROM employee_scd2 GROUP BY employee_id HAVING COUNT(*)>1 ORDER BY employee_id;

title: Successful transaction rate by payment method
prompt: For each payment_method, calculate the percentage of transactions with status = 'Success'. Return payment_method and success_rate_percent rounded to 2 decimals.
hint: Use SUM(CASE WHEN status='Success' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*).
sql: SELECT payment_method,ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN status='Success' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),2) AS success_rate_percent FROM transactions GROUP BY payment_method ORDER BY payment_method;

title: Employees with failed logins
prompt: Find employees who have at least one failed login. Return employee_id and failed_login_count.
hint: Filter login_status = 'Failed', group by employee_id, count rows.
sql: SELECT employee_id,COUNT(*) AS failed_login_count FROM login_history WHERE login_status='Failed' GROUP BY employee_id ORDER BY employee_id;

title: Login duration
prompt: For successful logins with a logout time, calculate hours_logged between login_time and logout_time. Return employee_id, login_time and hours_logged rounded to 2 decimals.
hint: SQLite's julianday() can calculate the difference between timestamps.
sql: SELECT employee_id,login_time,ROUND((julianday(logout_time)-julianday(login_time))*24,2) AS hours_logged FROM login_history WHERE login_status='Success' AND logout_time IS NOT NULL ORDER BY login_time;

title: Weekend vs weekday revenue
prompt: Using date_calendar, compare total net revenue for weekend and weekday sales. Return is_weekend and revenue.
hint: Join sales.sale_date to date_calendar.full_date and group by is_weekend.
sql: SELECT d.is_weekend,SUM(s.net_amount) AS revenue FROM sales s JOIN date_calendar d ON s.sale_date=d.full_date GROUP BY d.is_weekend ORDER BY d.is_weekend;

title: Patients with multiple admissions
prompt: Find patients who were admitted more than once. Return patient_id and admission_count.
hint: Count admissions per patient and filter counts greater than 1.
sql: SELECT p.patient_id,p.patient_name,COUNT(a.admission_id) AS admission_count FROM patients p JOIN admissions a ON p.patient_id=a.patient_id GROUP BY p.patient_id,p.patient_name HAVING COUNT(a.admission_id)>1 ORDER BY p.patient_id;

title: Hospital admissions: max, min and average visits
prompt: Return one row containing max_visits, min_visits and average_visits from admissions. Round average_visits to 2 decimals.
hint: Use MAX, MIN and ROUND(AVG(...),2) without GROUP BY.
sql: SELECT MAX(number_of_visits) AS max_visits,MIN(number_of_visits) AS min_visits,ROUND(AVG(number_of_visits),2) AS average_visits FROM admissions;

title: Salesperson with highest total revenue
prompt: Find the employee who generated the highest total net sales. Return employee_id, employee_name and total_revenue.
hint: Join employees to sales, aggregate by employee, sort revenue descending and take one row.
sql: SELECT e.employee_id,e.employee_name,SUM(s.net_amount) AS total_revenue FROM employees e JOIN sales s ON e.employee_id=s.employee_id GROUP BY e.employee_id,e.employee_name ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 1;

title: Top 2 salespeople in each region
prompt: Calculate each salesperson's total revenue within each region, rank salespeople inside the region, and return only the top 2 per region.
hint: First aggregate revenue by employee and region. Then rank that aggregated result.
sql: WITH r AS (SELECT s.region,e.employee_id,e.employee_name,SUM(s.net_amount) AS revenue FROM sales s JOIN employees e ON s.employee_id=e.employee_id GROUP BY s.region,e.employee_id,e.employee_name), ranked AS (SELECT r.*,DENSE_RANK() OVER(PARTITION BY region ORDER BY revenue DESC) AS rnk FROM r) SELECT region,employee_id,employee_name,revenue,rnk FROM ranked WHERE rnk<=2 ORDER BY region,rnk,employee_name;

title: Orders above the customer's average order value
prompt: Return orders whose total_amount is greater than that customer's average order amount across all their orders. Return order_id, customer_id and total_amount.
hint: Compare each order to AVG(total_amount) for the same customer.
sql: SELECT o.order_id,o.customer_id,o.total_amount FROM orders o WHERE o.total_amount>(SELECT AVG(x.total_amount) FROM orders x WHERE x.customer_id=o.customer_id) ORDER BY o.customer_id,o.total_amount DESC;

title: Customers with both an order and a successful payment
prompt: Return customers who have at least one order and at least one successful transaction. Return unique customer_id and customer_name.
hint: EXISTS can express both conditions without multiplying rows.
sql: SELECT c.customer_id,c.customer_name FROM customers c WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id=c.customer_id) AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM transactions t WHERE t.customer_id=c.customer_id AND t.status='Success') ORDER BY c.customer_id;

title: Employees hired in the same year as their manager
prompt: Find employees whose hire year is the same as their manager's hire year. Return employee_name, employee_hire_date and manager_name.
hint: Join on manager_id and compare the year portions of the dates.
sql: SELECT e.employee_name,e.hire_date AS employee_hire_date,m.manager_name,m.hire_date AS manager_hire_date FROM employees e JOIN managers m ON e.manager_id=m.manager_id WHERE substr(e.hire_date,1,4)=substr(m.hire_date,1,4) ORDER BY e.employee_id;

title: Department with the highest headcount
prompt: Find the department with the highest number of employees. Return department_name and employee_count.
hint: Count employees by department and sort descending.
sql: SELECT d.department_name,COUNT(e.employee_id) AS employee_count FROM departments d JOIN employees e ON d.department_id=e.department_id GROUP BY d.department_id,d.department_name ORDER BY employee_count DESC,d.department_name LIMIT 1;

title: First and latest order date per customer
prompt: For every customer who has ordered, return customer_id, first_order_date and latest_order_date.
hint: GROUP BY customer_id and use MIN/MAX on order_date.
sql: SELECT c.customer_id,MIN(o.order_date) AS first_order_date,MAX(o.order_date) AS latest_order_date FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id=o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id ORDER BY c.customer_id;

title: Compare stored order total with item-derived total
prompt: Find orders where the stored orders.total_amount differs from the total calculated from order_items by more than 1. Return order_id, stored_total, calculated_total and difference.
hint: Aggregate item totals first, then compare the result with orders.total_amount.
sql: WITH x AS (SELECT order_id,ROUND(SUM(quantity*unit_price*(1-discount_pct/100.0)),2) AS calculated_total FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id) SELECT o.order_id,o.total_amount AS stored_total,x.calculated_total,ROUND(o.total_amount-x.calculated_total,2) AS difference FROM orders o JOIN x ON o.order_id=x.order_id WHERE ABS(o.total_amount-x.calculated_total)>1 ORDER BY o.order_id;

title: Latest salary record for each employee
prompt: From salaries, return only the latest salary record for each employee. Return employee_id, salary, effective_from and effective_to.
hint: ROW_NUMBER partitioned by employee_id ordered by effective_from DESC.
sql: SELECT employee_id,salary,effective_from,effective_to FROM (SELECT s.*,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY employee_id ORDER BY effective_from DESC) rn FROM salaries s) x WHERE rn=1 ORDER BY employee_id;

title: Three highest order values with ties
prompt: Return every order whose total_amount belongs to the top 3 distinct order values. If multiple orders share the same amount, include all of them.
hint: DENSE_RANK over total_amount DESC gives the required distinct-value ranking.
sql: SELECT order_id,customer_id,total_amount,order_value_rank FROM (SELECT order_id,customer_id,total_amount,DENSE_RANK() OVER(ORDER BY total_amount DESC) AS order_value_rank FROM orders) x WHERE order_value_rank<=3 ORDER BY order_value_rank,order_id;
